title: Can You Get From a to b?

concept.title: Label every node with its component once; each question is a comparison of two labels
body: Two nodes are connected exactly when they are in the same **component**. If there are many questions "can you get from `a` to `b`?", searching the graph for each question would cost O(n + m) every time. It is much better to **prepare once**: run the component search of the first task and give every node a **label**, the number of its component. Then each question is a comparison of two numbers, in O(1).

The label array replaces the "seen" array, because 0 means "not labelled yet" and any positive number is both "seen" and the name of the component. This "preprocess once, answer many questions fast" pattern is everywhere: the same idea with a disjoint-set structure (union-find) is used when edges are added over time.

statement: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `m` edges. Then `q` questions follow, each with two nodes `a` and `b`. For every question print `yes` if there is a walk from `a` to `b` along the edges (a node is connected to itself), and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
The next line has `q`, the number of questions.
Each of the next `q` lines has two nodes `a` and `b`.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The nodes 1 and 4 are connected; node 6 has no edges, so it is connected only to itself.

hints: Label every node with the number of its component, using one search per component.
Two nodes are connected exactly when their labels are equal.
Answer each question by comparing two labels.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]
q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

# Your code here

explanation: One search per component gives every node the number of its component; a question is answered by comparing the labels of its two nodes.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m + q), space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]
q = int(input())
qs = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
label = [0] * (n + 1)
count = 0
for start in range(1, n + 1):
    if label[start]:
        continue
    count += 1
    label[start] = count
    queue = [start]
    for v in queue:
        for w in adj[v]:
            if not label[w]:
                label[w] = count
                queue.append(w)
print("\n".join("yes" if label[a] == label[b] else "no" for a, b in qs))
